messages.author: b17f4d0880547804
messages.subject: unused argument (refresh = 100) rstan 2.8.1
parts:
Hi guys,
I was testing some models I had written on a new computer and installed a fresh copy of rstan and I've found that between 2.8.0 to 2.8.1 the refresh argument seems to no longer be used.

```
 Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  unused argument (refresh = 100) 
```

When I call stan using


```
stan(model_code = model, 
                        data = stan_data,
                        pars = c("full_data", "sigma_log_census","sigma_log_plot","sigma_log_ind","sigma_log_obs","log_alpha","y_censored","log_b_otc","log_census_error","log_plot_error","log_ind_error"), 
                        chains = 3,
                        control=list(adapt_delta=0.99,stepsize=0.005, max_treedepth =15),
                        iter = 2000, 
                        refresh=100))
```

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: unused argument (refresh = 100) rstan 2.8.1
parts:
On Sunday, November 22, 2015 at 5:56:04 PM UTC-5, James Camac wrote:
Hi guys,
I was testing some models I had written on a new computer and installed a fresh copy of rstan and I've found that between 2.8.0 to 2.8.1 the refresh argument seems to no longer be used.

```
 Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  unused argument (refresh = 100) 
```

It looks like refresh is getting passed to the parser, which does not use it. We'll fix it in December. If the refresh rate is that important to you, you can probably work around this issue by calling stan_model() then sampling(*, refresh = 100).

Ben
